keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «우주에서 날아온 거대한 암석이 공룡을 사라지게 한 재앙을 일으켰다(원인)» 와 «새는 사실 살아남은 공룡의 한 종류다(놀라운 사실)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the cause (a huge rock from space caused the disaster) and the surprise (birds are actually a kind of dinosaur that survived). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: A huge asteroid crashed into the Earth
Most dinosaurs died out, but birds survived

sumHowto.ko: 먼저 위 세 칸을 보고, 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 고르세요.
sumHowto.en: Look at the three boxes, then choose the right word for each blank.

qs.q: Why did many plants die after the asteroid crash?
qs.qko: 소행성이 충돌한 뒤 왜 많은 식물이 죽었나요?
opts: Because they could not get any sunlight
Because the dinosaurs ate all of them
Because the sea water became too salty
evs: Without sunlight, many plants died, and the animals that ate them starved.
But here is the surprise: not all dinosaurs disappeared.
It was about 10 kilometers wide, which is wider than Mount Everest is tall.
For more than 150 million years, dinosaurs ruled the Earth.
why: «햇빛이 없어서 많은 식물이 죽었다» 고 했어요. 충돌로 생긴 먼지구름이 햇빛을 가렸기 때문이에요.
The text says that without sunlight, many plants died. Clouds of dust from the crash blocked the sunlight.

qs.q: What does “mass extinction” mean in this text?
qs.qko: 이 글에서 «mass extinction» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: a time when a huge number of kinds of living things die out
a time when animals move to a new home
a time when many new plants start to grow
evs: About three out of four kinds of living things on Earth died out.
But here is the surprise: not all dinosaurs disappeared.
The end of the dinosaurs also gave small mammals, like our ancestors, a chance to spread.
Scientists call this kind of rock an asteroid.
why: 바로 앞 문장에서 지구 생물 종류의 약 4분의 3이 사라졌다고 했고, 이 사건을 «mass extinction» 이라고 불러요. 아주 많은 종류의 생물이 한꺼번에 사라지는 일이에요.
The sentence before says about three out of four kinds of living things died out. This event is called a mass extinction.

qs.q: Why can we say that not all dinosaurs disappeared?
qs.qko: 왜 공룡이 모두 사라진 것은 아니라고 말할 수 있나요?
opts: Because birds are a kind of dinosaur, and birds such as pigeons still live today
Because some big dinosaurs still hide in deep forests
Because the asteroid did not hit the Earth
evs: Scientists say that birds are actually a kind of dinosaur that survived.
So the next time you see a pigeon, remember that you are looking at a dinosaur!
Then, about 66 million years ago, almost all of them suddenly disappeared.
The crash made a crater, a giant hole, more than 150 kilometers across.
why: 과학자들은 새가 살아남은 공룡의 한 종류라고 말해요. 그래서 비둘기를 보면 공룡을 보고 있는 것이라고 했어요. 두 문장을 이어야 해요.
Scientists say birds are a kind of dinosaur that survived, so a pigeon is a living dinosaur. You need both sentences.

ends: How do scientists learn about dinosaurs from fossils?
과학자들은 화석으로 공룡에 대해 어떻게 알아낼까?
In what ways are birds like dinosaurs?

write.src: “I want to <u>see a real dinosaur fossil</u> because <u>I want to know how big dinosaurs were</u>.”
write.howtoKo: 예문을 틀로 삼아, 빈칸 두 곳을 «하고 싶은 일 + 그 이유» 로 바꿔 영어로 써 보세요.
write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write what you want to do and your reason in English.
write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을» 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because birds are living dinosaurs)
write.moreEn: One more step: after «because», write who + what to make your reason clear. (e.g. because birds are living dinosaurs)
